method: All eight final PNGs and all sixteen distinct native-model-derived reference PNGs were opened individually with view_image(detail=original), in four batches of six images. Files were not edited. Byte hashes were independently compared with the current sprite manifest and tool-artifact bindings.

reviews.sourceEdition: Resident Evil 2 — port GameCube (2003), Zombie Dog
observations: Four source views show a lean black/rust dog with long legs, pointed ears, an open muzzle and a short tapering tail. Exact side projections occlude the far legs; frontal/rear views provide the other views, not a walking sequence.
Both generated sides retain this overall source presentation and do not add equipment. The open mouth, near ear, tail end and visible paws can be followed visually within the supplied canvas.

The right-facing output shows the rightward muzzle and the relatively dark/rust near foreleg marking seen in the corresponding native side. Its teeth and outlined face are reconstructed details rather than verified original texels.
appearanceReservations: A diffuse brown halo/glow is visible around the generated silhouettes, particularly the head and paws, whereas the preserved native reference views have clean subject contours.

Thin dark outlining, texture enlargement, lighting and reconstructed mouth/eye details prevent a pixel-equivalence claim. Hidden leg articulation and four-limb separation in the side projection remain unverified.
reviews.poseQualification: Two separately supplied static source-guided presentations, not a native frame or a fluent original idle.
reviews.clippingAssessmentBasis: Direct visual inspection of the original complete PNG, tracing visible body extremities; no blanket completeness claim is inferred from an alpha bounding box. Faint fringes and hidden anatomy remain unverified.

observations: The four source views show an elongated olive/green reptile with a very long tapering tail, slightly open toothed muzzle, plated/scaly skin and vertically presented near legs. Far limbs are occluded in the exact side projections.

Both generated sides retain the long head-to-tail profile, low body and unarmed animal presentation. Tail tips, muzzle ends and visible feet are visually identifiable within the images; no obvious principal body cut was observed.

The right-facing output keeps the tail taper to the left, snout to the right and visible near fore/hind feet beneath the body. The near eye/teeth/scales are more resolved and differently lit than the small native render, so their exact correspondence is unverified.

reviews.sourceEdition: Resident Evil 2 — port GameCube (2003), Giant Moth
observations: The source views show an ochre/brown tapered insect body with compacted wings, a dark eye, antennae and thin hanging legs. They do not show an expanded-wing flight pose.

The generated pair retains that compact body/wing presentation and long narrow extremities rather than inventing a spread-wing phase. The main antenna, abdomen tip and visible leg tips are identifiable within each image.

The right-facing image places the dark eye and antenna toward the right with three visible thin limb forms beneath the forebody and the tapered abdomen at the left. Its enlarged golden texture and cap-like thorax are source-guided but not exact original pixels.
appearanceReservations: Red/yellow coloured edge fringes are visibly present around several leg, antenna and body contours in both generated images.
Brightness, texture reconstruction, thin appendage thickness and occluded topology are not certified 1:1 with the native model render.
reviews.poseQualification: Static compact-wing source presentation only; no flight, locomotion, original idle role or combat animation is proved.

reviews.sourceEdition: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis — port GameCube (2003), blonde female costume1
observations: The four source views show an adult blonde female with short hair, dark sleeveless collared/buttoned top, beige straight skirt around the knees, dark ankle straps/shoes and asymmetric skin/costume markings.

Both generated outputs retain the broad costume and visible head, hands, skirt hem and shoes. Arms moved forward, slightly flexed knees and separated feet are clearly an adapted neutral stance rather than the original arms-down source pose.

The right-facing output shows the profile, darker sleeveless top, beige hem, two relaxed forward hands and strapped shoes with readable shoe tips. Face, visible hand detail, garment folds and source markings are reconstructed; exact native texture correspondence is not established.
appearanceReservations: A diffuse brown halo is visible around the generated body and lower legs, plus a thin dark contour not present as such in the reference views.
Face/hair smoothing, skin-mark texture placement, bracelets, folds and source geometry cannot be certified exactly; the stance change must remain labelled as an adaptation.
reviews.poseQualification: Two generated static stance adaptations, not original game poses, sprites or fluent idle animation.

sourceAcquisitionScope: Reference images come from the already preserved GameCube model archives and derived source views. Historical archive HTTP200 metadata is not a claim of newly successful source-page access; currently denied source pages are not bypassed.
limitations: No image was approved as a native/original-game sprite or a geometrically/pixel-exact1:1 reproduction.
Diffuse brown halos/added outlining in the dog and female zombie images, and visible coloured edge fringes especially around the moth, remain observed differences from the native references.
This standalone review does not verify an animation, original idle role, hidden anatomy, physical scale or PlayStation/GameCube equivalence.

Only the supplied images were reviewed here; current in-game placement, animation playback, GPU/physical-screen output and underlying model authenticity were not independently certified by this visual inspection.
